answer: Physical Provenance Ledger. Each identity registers a sonnet of hardware attestations: a signed hash chain from a tamper-resistant secure element, counter-signed by the silicon foundry at wafer test. A vault of these chains is checked against known fab records, so a clone lacks a valid die signature. Operators must purchase distinct physical dies and pass remote attestation within a ledge of tolerance for clock drift; faking requires acquiring real silicon at foundry cost per identity.
